title: Fix provider binding validation: tolerate runtime model-selections rewrite when payload matches
refined_problem: validate_provider_active (scripts/harnesslib.py) rejects any provider binding whose recorded byte-sha of model-selections.json no longer matches the file, but the OpenCode runtime itself rewrites that file whenever agent model state updates (observed: every orchestrator turn invalidated the binding, blocking receipt_review.prepare --apply and re-activation of MVP-EVAL-001). The very next check (line 305) already compares the selections payload semantically; the byte-sha check makes legitimate runtime self-updates indistinguishable from tampering and deadlocks the control plane.

original_request.text: sequence of failed prepare --apply with 'provider active binding model selections integrity mismatch' even when activation and prepare ran back-to-back in the operator shell; orchestrator session activity rewrites model-selections.json between steps

target_users: Harness operators running long-lived OpenCode sessions
Orchestrator agents closing tasks that require binding validation
outcomes: Binding validation tolerates a model-selections file rewritten by the runtime when the selections payload is semantically identical to the binding
receipt_review.prepare --apply and provider activation no longer deadlock in live sessions
success_metrics: New regression test reproduces the drift (mutate model-selections.json payload-identically, e.g. re-serialize same selections with different key order/indentation) and validation accepts it
A payload-divergent tamper (selections changed) is still rejected

in: scripts/harnesslib.py validate_provider_active: on sha mismatch, fall back to semantic equality of the selections payload (active['selections'] == selection_payload['selections']) before rejecting; document the decision in a comment
New regression test file covering both directions (payload-equal drift accepted; payload-divergent rejected)
out: Changes to .opencode/plugins (TypeScript plugin keeps its own stricter check; it fails closed on logs without blocking gates)
Changes to activation flow, task router, or policy files

mvp.goal: Unblock receipt_review.prepare and task closure in live sessions without weakening tamper detection.

success_metrics_note: Deterministic tests only; no live-session dependence.
assumptions: The runtime rewrite preserves the selections payload (model ids unchanged) - verified by the equality check at line 305 being the intended second line of defense
Tampering with model payloads remains rejected by both the sha and the payload checks
challenges: Keeping the fix minimal and reviewable: one function, one condition, clear comment

tasks.title: Semantic fallback for provider binding model-selections validation
tasks.description: In scripts/harnesslib.py validate_provider_active: replace the hard raise at the sha mismatch (line ~303) with a fallback: if active['model_selections_sha256'] != selection_hash, accept when active.get('selections') == selection_payload.get('selections') (semantic identity; the runtime rewrote the file payload-identically); otherwise raise the integrity error. Add comment explaining the decision. Add the regression test at backend/tests/test_binding_drift.py (NOT tests/ at repo root): the deterministic check-runner derives the project root and its per-project unittest timeout from task files, and a task whose files include a repo-root tests/ path resolves project root to the repository root, whose full suite (~9-10 min) exceeds the runner's hardcoded 60s per-command cap (no override knob exists) - placing the regression test under the backend project makes the gate deterministic and fast (~2s). The test imports harnesslib via sys.path insert of the repo-root scripts directory. Two regression tests: (1) payload-identical re-serialization validates; (2) a selections payload change still raises. All existing backend tests must pass.
acceptance_criteria: validate_provider_active accepts a binding whose model-selections file was re-serialized payload-identically (different bytes, same selections)
validate_provider_active still rejects payload-divergent model-selections files (different selections content)
backend/tests/test_binding_drift.py contains the two regression tests (plus T0 control and T3 characterization) and passes under both python -m unittest discover -s tests -v and pytest from backend/
Whole backend test suite passes unchanged (~fast; the root-level tests/ suite is out of scope for this task's gate)
No changes outside scripts/harnesslib.py and backend/tests/test_binding_drift.py
Comment documents why the fallback exists (runtime self-rewrite, semantic second line of defense) and the test docstring documents the placement rationale (check-runner project-root timeout model)

research_rdd.reason: Root cause already diagnosed with exact code-line evidence in this session (harnesslib.py:303 vs runtime rewrite behavior).

recorded_decisions: owner asked to unblock and continue; the deadlock reproduced deterministically across three attempts (two in operator shell without plugin interference)
semantic fallback preserves tamper detection (payload divergence still rejected); plugin unchanged

2026-11-12 rescope (evidence-driven): the task_checks per-command timeout (60000 ms, hardcoded, no override) cannot accommodate a repo-root tests/ suite (~9-10 min measured with 300s-capped attempts where all tests passed up to each cut point); the regression test therefore moves to backend/tests/test_binding_drift.py (project-root gate model) and the task_checks timeout hunk is dropped from scope, recorded as known limitation + backlog (root-suite timeout support needs proper per-task design)
this fix is self-bootstrapping: prepare/import loads harnesslib fresh, so MVP-EVAL-001 closes with the fixed validator
